main_text.l: Deltale adfcribitur literæ ت poft ذ, ut وَجَدْتُ wajatto inveni.
Lamdale, poft ل articuli اَلْ, ut اَلرَّبِّ
arrabbo Dominus, اَللّٰه allaho ὁ Θεὸς.
Lam vero articularis sæpè omittitur, cùm
solaris eum sequitur ٱلَّيْلُ ut ٱللَّيْلُ allailo,
pro ٱللَّيْلِ: & hoc perpetuum est in relati-vis, ٱلَّذِي ٱلَّتِي &
ٱلدِّينِ, & cùm ar-ticulo præfigitur ل datívi casûs nota, ne tria
Lam concurrant, ut لِلَّهِ Deo, pro لِلَّهِ[?].
- Initiale est quod apponitur literis لَوْمِين[?]
vel expressum, ut مِن رَبِّ[?] mirrabbi-hi
à domino suo, vel latens in vocali nunna-ta,

page.notes: The Arabic letters in the first example ("literæ ت", "وَجَدْتُ") and the vowel marks on the Arabic words are hard to read at this scan resolution and may not be exact. The "solaris" in the third paragraph is printed with a letter that looks like f; I read it as s, since long s is transcribed as plain s. The page is cut off after "relati-", and the text continues on the next part. Arabic words are copied as far as they can be read; forms marked [?] are doubtful. The Arabic at the start of the first line is hard to order and may be misplaced.
